lectures.title: Digital platforms and portals in news

parts.t: Panchayati Raj and rural water platforms
items: Ministry of Panchayati Raj, NIC and DigiHaat
Voluntary citizen-participation platform enabling citizens and organisations to donate verified digital-equipment bundles to eligible Gram Panchayats. Tagline: “Give Back to Your Village.”
Provides access to Panchayat finances, plans, development works and public assets. Integrated with DigiHaat for DAANVEER.
Panchayat planning, budgeting, accounting, progress reporting, asset management and online payments.
Panchayat Advancement Index; evaluates Gram Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies through measurable indicators. Launched 26 May 2025.
Digital platform associated with Gram Sabha and Panchayat meetings.
Supports Gram Panchayat Development Plan preparation and monitoring.
GIS-based spatial planning and decision-support platform.
Digital portal related to self-reliant Panchayats; launched 27 July 2026.
Integrated national digital platform for mapping rural water-supply systems from source to household tap. Each village is assigned a unique Sujal village/service-area ID.

parts.t: State platforms: Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
items: Brings the work of all 48 State departments onto one digital platform to improve transparency and accountability.
Launched alongside the Sankalp Dashboard on 13 October 2026.
Unified digital platform for public services; contract of ₹87 crore awarded to Corporate Infotech Pvt. Ltd.
Centralised Grievance Redressal and Monitoring platform, launched 5 June 2026.
Public grievance-redressal platform launched 11 May 2026, with toll-free helpline 1100.
Digital platform designed to simplify and improve the investor experience; launched 24 March 2026.
Journey of Antenatal, Natal and Neonatal Integrated Care. Digital platform for maternal and child healthcare, longitudinal health records and real-time monitoring.
Vaccination platform for session planning, registration, recording and reporting.
Integrated platform bringing multiple national health programmes onto a single digital interface.
One-stop platform for AB PM-JAY beneficiaries, including eligibility verification and beneficiary services.
Digital platform for standardised exchange of health insurance claim information.
Interoperable digital-health framework connecting citizens with healthcare service providers.
Secure and governed platform for analysing health data generated under AB PM-JAY and ABDM.
Redesigned citizen-facing digital health platform under ABDM, with ABHA creation, health-record management and access to digital health services.
**BODH:** Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI. Developed by IIT Kanpur with the National Health Authority (NHA).
**BODH – purpose:** privacy-preserving Health AI benchmarking and validation platform; enables evaluation of AI models using anonymised real-world health data.
**SAHI:** Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India; the national strategy for AI in healthcare, a framework for safe and responsible AI use in healthcare.
AI-based agricultural digital public infrastructure intended to provide farmers with integrated agricultural information and support.
AI model using satellite imagery to identify field boundaries, trees, woodlands, wells and small irrigation structures.
AI model for identifying crop activity, likely crops, sowing and harvesting periods.
Uses ALU API with Gemini to provide field-level agricultural insights, including for sustainable rice cultivation.
Initiative listed among the outcomes of the 18th BRICS Summit 2026; promotes digital cooperation in agriculture.
**BRICS Centres of Excellence on Agro-Ecology and Regenerative Agriculture**
BRICS cooperation initiative focused on agro-ecology and regenerative agriculture.
Digital cooperation initiative for micro, small and medium enterprises.
Platform for cooperation and support for start-ups and innovation.
BRICS initiative related to skill development and cooperation.
Works on interoperability among payment and financial messaging systems. No common BRICS currency was announced.
**BRICS Digital Centre of Excellence for Smart Grids and Energy Storage**
Launched at the 11th BRICS Energy Ministers Meeting in Gurugram, 25–26 June 2026.
Open-source AI platform for education, including personalised AI tutors, AI-assisted teacher training and institutional administration.
IIT Madras-incubated initiative associated with the development of Bharat EduAI Stack.
Uttar Pradesh Skill Development Mission platform for paperless registration and empanelment of training partners.
Provides district-wise information on training centres, courses, locations and contact details through an interactive digital map.
Approved for Patna to support youth seeking overseas employment; described as an institutional facility rather than a software platform.
**Bihar Vidya Saathi:** 24×7 one-to-one interactive learning platform for students in approximately 700 designated model schools in Bihar.
**Bihar Vidya Saathi – coverage:** Classes 9–10 and the science stream in Classes 11–12, integrating teacher support, digital resources and AI tools.
Digital India BHASHINI Division under MeitY; multilingual, voice-enabled digital public services.
IndiaAI initiative for AI datasets and models.
National AI initiative and ecosystem supporting AI development and adoption.
National Innovation Challenge for Drone Application and Research; launched by MeitY and Drone Federation India on 13 July 2026 under SwaYaan.
**Global Call for Control of Frontier AI Models**
International initiative launched in New York on 21 September 2026 to promote human oversight and control of advanced AI models.
**Languages:** supports more than 36 languages in text and over 22 languages in voice.
**AI models:** has deployed more than 350 AI language models.
**Applications:** translation, speech recognition and conversational AI.
**Showcased** at the AI-Led Innovation and Capacity Building Conference in Lucknow on 20 January 2026.
Digital-payment platform; BHIM App integration with Tatkal NPS, and Mahendra Singh Dhoni as its brand ambassador.
Payment platform associated with international interoperability initiatives involving Uzbekistan and Seychelles.
Provides a platform for global dialogue, collaboration and innovation in financial technology.
**GFF 2026 theme:** “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI | Tokenisation | Quantum: Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.”
**Bharat Taxi** is India's first cooperative-led ride-hailing platform, based on “Driver is the Owner”.
**Services:** cab, auto, bike and rental services.
**Drivers:** participating drivers are called **Saarthis** (also spelt Sarathis).
**Features:** driver and vehicle verification, trip records, SOS and journey-sharing features.
**Launch:** at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, in February 2026.
Platform for cooperation among member countries on trade, finance, development, technology and global governance.
International forum for economic cooperation and global policy coordination.
Platform for cooperation on UN Security Council reform.
Multilateral platform for international trade rules and dispute settlement.
Open, voluntary platform promoting international law, peace, cooperation and institutional reform. Launched 21 September 2026 in New York.
Voluntary cooperation platform focused on shipping safety, maritime security and seafarers' welfare.
Knowledge bridge and people-to-people platform celebrating the cultural, spiritual and intellectual links between Tamil Nadu and Kashi.
120 mm mortar mounted on a mobile vehicle platform; intended to provide battlefield mobility and firepower.
Guided-missile frigate programme; ships have platform-management systems alongside improved stealth, automation, sensors, weapons and survivability.
GaN-based semiconductor devices are discussed for radar, electronic warfare, communication and other defence applications.
Skyroot Aerospace's orbital launch vehicle; completed its first successful private orbital launch in July 2026.
Pixxel and Sarvam orbital data-centre satellite concept; intended to enable AI processing in orbit.
TakeMe2Space orbital computing satellite; AI data processing in orbit.
**I-2SEA submarine cable system:** digital connectivity infrastructure linking India, Southeast Asia and data-centre hubs in the region.
**I-2SEA – route:** submarine cable infrastructure for connectivity between India, Malaysia and Singapore, with onward connection to Hyderabad and Chennai.

lectures.title: Defence: Vision 2047, missiles, technology and exercises of 2026

items: **Defence Forces Vision 2047:** released by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh on 10 March 2026, at South Block, New Delhi.
**Full title:** Defence Forces Vision 2047: A Roadmap for a Future-Ready Indian Military.
**Prepared by:** Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS).
**Objective:** transform India's armed forces into a modern, integrated, technologically advanced and self-reliant military by the centenary of Independence.
Ministry of Defence declared 2025 as the “Year of Reforms” to promote jointness, integration and future-readiness
2030–2040: deeper integration of cyber and space capabilities; operationalisation of layered air and missile defence systems
2040–2047: fully integrated, self-reliant, all-domain military force
Successfully tested for the first time on 23 July 2026; tested from APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha
Flight-tested on 8 July 2026 at Integrated Test Range, Chandipur; tested for a minimum strike range of 60 km
Test-fired on 6 February 2026 at ITR, Chandipur, Odisha; range given as 3,000–3,500 km
Under development; described as capable of high-speed manoeuvres at high altitudes, exceeding Mach 5
Successfully demonstrated on 3 February 2026 at ITR, Chandipur, Odisha
**What it is:** indigenous modular range-extension kit for low-cost aerial weapons.
**Developer:** designed and developed by Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad, along with other DRDO laboratories.
**Trial:** maiden flight trial on 7 May 2026; jointly trialled by DRDO and the Indian Air Force.
**Objective:** improve the combat value of low-cost aerial weapons.
**TARA** is described as India's first indigenous glide weapon system for converting unguided warheads into precision-guided weapons.
**Ahuti Mk II:** electric multirotor interceptor of Apollyon Dynamics, Hyderabad; recorded test speed of 498 km/h.
**Ahuti Mk II – record:** confirmed 29 August 2026 and published 1 September 2026.
**KAL:** indigenous long-range one-way attack drone of IG Defence, Noida; flight trial at Pokhran Field Firing Range, Rajasthan.
**Full form:** Situational Awareness for Kinetic Soft and Hard Kill Assets Management.
**Objective:** detect, track, identify and neutralise enemy drones, quadcopters and unmanned aerial systems in real time in border areas.
**User:** the Indian Army, which initiated procurement.
India Optel Limited / Ordnance Factory, Dehradun
Indigenous high-resolution binoculars launched on 13 August 2026; 8× magnification, 7.6° field of view, approximately 610 g
120 mm vehicle-mounted mortar and bomb system demonstrated to the Indian Army at Infantry School, Mhow, on 17 June 2026
Designed by GTRE; Azad Engineering identified as industry partner; engine realised and delivered to GTRE on 22 July 2026
Integrated application launched in May 2026 for logistics and sustainment management
**GaN** stands for Gallium Nitride; used in high-frequency and high-power applications. Organisations: DRDO / SSPL / GAETEC.
**Chip:** a single indigenous chip measuring 3.5 × 3 mm can deliver up to 30 watts.
**SSPL:** DRDO's Solid State Physics Laboratory developed indigenous processes for manufacturing 4-inch Silicon Carbide (SiC) wafers.
**SSPL fabricated:** GaN HEMTs with power capabilities up to 150 watts, and MMICs up to 40 watts for applications up to X-band frequencies.
**GAETEC, Hyderabad:** limited production capability for indigenous GaN-on-SiC MMICs established there.

**iDEX contract:** under Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX), a contract was signed with Agnit Semiconductors Private Limited to develop advanced GaN semiconductors for next-generation defence wireless transmitters.
**Applications:** radars, electronic warfare, communications, intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and unmanned systems.

lectures.title: Central schemes and programmes in news

items: **Full form:** Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act. Ministry of Rural Development.
**VB-G RAM G Act** came into force across rural India on 1 July 2026, replacing the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 (MGNREGA).
**Employment guarantee:** increased from 100 to 125 days per financial year.
**Wage floor:** notified minimum wage floor for 2026–27 is ₹300 per day.
**Four priority areas:** 1. Water security; 2. Rural infrastructure; 3. Livelihood infrastructure; 4. Climate resilience.
Other States and UTs with legislatures
**Total expected outlay** including State share: over ₹1.51 lakh crore.
**Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS):** MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology); notified 8 April 2025.
**ECMS – scope:** supports domestic manufacturing of electronic components, materials and production (manufacturing) equipment.
**ECMS – outlay:** initial outlay ₹22,919 crore, increased to ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026–27.
**Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS):** MeitY; Cabinet approval on 15 July 2026; notification on 21 August 2026.
**MPMS – outlay and period:** ₹62,500 crore; five-year period FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31.
**MPMS – aim:** expand mobile-phone production, domestic value addition and supply-chain resilience.
**PLI-LSEM:** Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Large-Scale Electronics Manufacturing (MeitY); predecessor to MPMS; ended on 31 March 2026.

**India Semiconductor Mission (MeitY):** two additional projects approved on 5 May 2026 in Gujarat, with cumulative investment of around ₹3,936 crore and expected employment for 2,230 skilled professionals.

**Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme:** ₹10,000 crore scheme of the Government of India announced in Union Budget 2026–27; intended to increase India's annual container manufacturing capacity to around 7.5 lakh TEUs.
Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products scheme extended up to 31 December 2026
Two new SEZs notified in Puducherry on 27 May 2026 to promote investment, manufacturing and jobs.
10 years of Startup India and the fifth National Startup Awards / States' Startup Ranking Framework.
Supports defence innovation and startups. iDEX contract with Agnit Semiconductors for advanced GaN semiconductors.
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited participated in the agreement for the proposed greenfield shipyard at Thoothukudi.
**Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI)**
Referred to in the 16th Finance Commission material in connection with State fiscal-deficit calculations.
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Approved by Union Cabinet on 18 March 2026.
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
**Modified UDAN:** Ministry of Civil Aviation; Cabinet approval on 25 March 2026.
**Period and outlay:** ten-year period, FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36; outlay ₹28,840 crore.
**Aim:** improve regional air connectivity and support airport infrastructure.
**Airports:** proposes development of 100 airports from existing unserved airstrips; ₹12,159 crore provision for this component over eight years.

**GOBARdhan:** organic waste-to-energy initiative; introduced in 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) to convert organic waste into biogas and bio-slurry; now consolidated as a Central Sector Scheme.
**GOBARdhan – Central Sector Scheme:** Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; Cabinet approval on 6 August 2026; formally launched on 1 October 2026.
**Outlay and period:** ₹23,731 crore for the implementation period FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36.
**What it does:** converts agricultural residue, cattle dung and municipal organic waste into compressed biogas, organic manure, employment and economic value.
Outlay ₹564.75 crore. By 16 March 2026, 37 proposals had received nearly ₹248 crore in approval for assistance.
Outlay ₹994.5 crore for FY 2024–25 to FY 2028–29; ₹56.31 crore sanctioned.
**Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen):** Ministry of Jal Shakti; launched in 2014.
**Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme:** Government of India; pilot projects began in 2001; programme launched in 2003 in nine States and four Union Territories.
**EBP milestones:** E10 achieved in June 2022; phased E20 rollout began on 6 February 2023.
**National Policy on Biofuels:** the 2018 policy targeted E20 by 2030; the 2022 amendment advanced the target to Ethanol Supply Year 2025–26.

**Bharat-VISTAAR:** AI-powered agricultural Digital Public Infrastructure of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare; a farmer-facing gateway, described as a single digital gateway for farmers.
**Bharat-VISTAAR – launch:** on 17 February 2026 in Jaipur by Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
**Bharat-VISTAAR – Phase 1:** in Hindi and English, with rollout in states including Maharashtra, Bihar and Gujarat.
Drone-based mapping of rural inhabited areas and preparation of property cards. As of January 2026, 3.06 crore property cards prepared across 1.86 lakh villages.
Connects rural women entrepreneurs with wider markets, buyers and business opportunities.
Supports fisheries development. Tamil Nadu's 3D-printed artificial reef pilot off Rameswaram under Phase II of the programme.
**Jal Jeevan Mission:** Ministry of Jal Shakti; launched on 15 August 2019; original target was tap-water connections for every rural household by 2024.
**JJM 2.0:** Cabinet approval on 10 March 2026; converts JJM from an infrastructure-creation model to a service-based model.
**Expenditure:** revised expenditure ₹8.69 lakh crore, including Central contribution of ₹3.59 lakh crore.
**JJM 2.0 target:** tap water to all 19.36 crore rural households by December 2028.
**Direction:** JJM 2.0 aims to move towards a utility-based service model and 24×7 rural drinking-water supply.
**Sujalam Bharat:** integrated digital platform; each village receives a unique Sujal village/service-area ID for mapping water supply from source to household tap.
**Jal Arpan:** Gram Panchayats and Village Water and Sanitation Committees participate in accountability and certification.
**Jal Utsav:** proposed annual programme to strengthen community participation.
**Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS):** Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; launched in December 2023.
**PRAMAAN certificates:** first presented on 29 September 2026, to Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation for plantations covering 33,000 hectares and to an Odisha farmer associated with OBDA.
**Project Cheetah:** Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change / NTCA; launched on 17 September 2022 at Kuno National Park.
**Project Cheetah – details:** cheetahs brought from Namibia and South Africa; expanded to Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary in 2025.
**Project Him Sarovar:** Ladakh Administration; water-security initiative designed for cold-desert conditions; focuses on scientific snow harvesting and water conservation.
**Namo Oxygen Parks:** Delhi Government / Ministry of Environment context; 18 parks inaugurated in Delhi on 5 June 2026 under green initiatives linked to the Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam campaign.

**Net Zero Portal / NAPCC Dashboard:** digital initiatives of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change launched on 16 September 2026 to strengthen climate-action transparency and coordination.
**Net Zero Portal / NAPCC Dashboard** are portals, not standalone financial schemes.

parts.t: Pensions, social assistance and food security
items: **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP):** Ministry of Rural Development; Cabinet approved continuation from FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31, with total outlay ₹53,428 crore over five years.
**NSAP – beneficiaries:** assistance to elderly persons, widows, persons with disabilities and eligible poor households.
**Atal Pension Yojana (APY):** pension / financial inclusion; Union Cabinet approved continuation up to FY 2030–31 on 21 January 2026.

**National Pension System (NPS):** PFRDA committee constituted on 13 January 2026 under Dr M. S. Sahoo to formulate guidelines for assured payouts. This is a reform exercise, not a new pension scheme.
**SARTHAK-PDS Scheme:** Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved continuation and integration on 27 May 2026; Central outlay ₹25,530 crore.
**SARTHAK-PDS – period:** implementation up to 31 March 2031, during the 16th Finance Commission award cycle.
**CBDC-based food subsidy distribution under PMGKAY:** listed as a current-affairs topic in the contents; the contents entry alone does not provide operational details.
**Delhi Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana:** Delhi Government; launched by President Droupadi Murmu on 2 March 2026.
**PM-RAHAT Scheme:** Government of India; launched on 13 February 2026 and officially named through notification on 19 February 2026.
**PM-RAHAT – benefit:** eligible road-accident victims get treatment cover up to ₹1.5 lakh for a maximum of seven days.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / NHA
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / NHA
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Women and Child Development
**Mission SEHAT:** ICAR and ICMR; connects agricultural science, nutrition research and public health; launched 11 May 2026.
**SAHI:** Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India; Health AI governance initiative launched 17 February 2026; a national guidance framework for responsible healthcare AI.
**BODH:** Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI (IIT Kanpur and NHA); privacy-preserving platform to evaluate AI models on anonymised health data.
**Aarogya Setu 2.0:** NHA / ABDM; launched 29 June 2026; redesigned as a personal health-record and citizen-facing digital health application.
**Ayushman App:** NHA; PM-JAY beneficiary eligibility, Ayushman Card services, treatment history, hospital discovery and grievance.
**Gyan Bharatam initiative:** Ministry of Culture; announced in Union Budget 2025–26.
**National Manuscript Survey:** launched on 16 March 2026 to identify, document and prepare for preservation and digitisation of manuscripts.
